title: Token cost attribution pipeline for per-route & per-model billing
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Background: Product and Finance need a reliable, low-latency pipeline to compute per-request token cost attribution and rollups by route, customer, and model. Current billing reports rely on coarse daily aggregates which miss spikes and do not reflect short-lived route-level surges. This ticket implements an always-correct, scalable pipeline that converts per-request telemetry (OTLP spans + per-token logs) into token counts, assigns costing metadata, and emits aggregated rollups suitable for billing, alerting, and cost dashboards.

Goals:
- Produce near-real-time per-route, per-model, and per-customer token usage metrics (1m granularity) labeled for billing and SLO calculations.
- Preserve request-level provenance for sampling/inspectability (store sampled traces with cost metadata).
- Keep downstream Prom/TSDB cardinality bounded via controlled rollups and tenant aggregation strategies.
- Integrate with existing billing engine (billing-aggregator) and Redwood Console dashboards.

Telemetry sources and inputs:
- OTLP traces: span events that mark "generation.start", "generation.token" (for streaming) and "generation.end". Spans contain model_id, route_id, billing_tier, and customer_id labels.
- Structured logs (ndjson) from runtime for per-token events when streaming is enabled (fallback for older runtimes).
- Prom counters emitted from runtime sidecars for token_count_total per model/route (used for reconciliation).

Design approach (high level):
1) Ingest: Collect OTLP traces and structured token logs into the telemetry Kafka topic (telemetry.inference.calls).
2) Enrich: A stream job (Flink) correlates spans and token events to construct canonical per-request objects: {request_id, model_id, route_id, customer_id, token_counts: {prompt, completion, total}, sequence_length_distribution}. Enrichment also applies price per token from product catalog (pull from pricing-service cache).
3) Reduce & rollup: Aggregate canonical objects into minute-level rollups with labels: [customer_id, model_id, route_id, pricing_tier, region]. Emit two outputs: low-cardinality Prom-style aggregates (remote write) and high-cardinality append-only billing events to ClickHouse/BigQuery for audit and dispute resolution.
4) Sampling & retention: Keep 0.5% deterministic sample of full request objects (configurable) with deterministic hashing on request_id -> stored in s3/ClickHouse for 90 days. Aggregates retained per current telemetry retention policy.
5) Backpressure & safety: If the enrichment job lags, write raw telemetry to a hot-journal S3 prefix and emit degraded-mode metrics (degraded_token_rollup=true) to Console with ETA for catchup.

Acceptance criteria:
- Pipeline processes synthetic load (10k req/s, avg 120 tokens/req) end-to-end with <60s delay to minute rollups and 99.9% delivery to Prom remote write.
- Aggregated per-minute metrics exposed as Prom time series with labels model_id, route_id and customer_id (customer_id only for enterprise tenants; for public tenants use customer_bucket label) to control cardinality.
- Deterministic sampled requests available for debugging via Console links in <2 min.
- Billing team validates parity (within 0.2%) vs. existing offline billing on a 24h reconciliation run for three pilot customers.
- Security review completed for PII handling and pricing cache access; KMS usage documented.

Implementation tasks:
- T1: Telemetry schema update: add canonical token events to OTLP span spec and runtime sidecar (PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/4217).
- T2: Ingest connector: kafka topic onboarding + schema registry (avro) (PR: github.com/redwood/telemetry/pull/238).
- T3: Flink enrichment job: join spans/logs -> canonical request object. Metric counters for lag/backpressure. (draft job at infra/flink/jobs/token_attrib).
- T4: Rollup writer: write both remote_write compatible metrics and append-only events to ClickHouse.
- T5: Sampling store and Console integration: deterministic sampler + link to trace in Console UI (frontend task in Console backlog).
- T6: QA/Load tests and reconciliation runs with billing.

Design trade-offs considered:
- Option A: Do full request reconstruction in streaming (chosen) vs Option B: approximate attribution from Prom counters + heuristics. We chose reconstruction to achieve precise per-request billing and dispute resolution.
- Storage: ClickHouse chosen for append-only audit table due to query speed on large volumes. S3 archival used for raw journal.
- Sampling rate default 0.5% to balance inspectability and storage; made configurable per-tenant.

Security & privacy notes:
- Customer identifiers will be hashed for public tenants in Prom outputs and only the billing pipeline has access to raw customer_id.
- Pricing cache access uses service identity with KMS key; support for customer-managed KMS will require a follow-up.
